var i = 1;
while (i <= 15) {
  if (i % 15 == 0) { console.log("FizzBuzz"); }
  else if (i % 3 == 0) { console.log("Fizz"); }
  else if (i % 5 == 0) { console.log("Buzz"); }
  else { console.log(i); }
  i = i + 1;
}
// FizzBuzz: the classic
for (let i = 1; i <= 30; i++) {
  if (i % 15 == 0) console.log("FizzBuzz");
  else if (i % 3 == 0) console.log("Fizz");
  else if (i % 5 == 0) console.log("Buzz");
  else console.log(i);
}
// the sieve of Eratosthenes
const n = 60;
let sieve = [];
for (let i = 0; i <= n; i++) sieve.push(true);
for (let p = 2; p * p <= n; p++) {
  if (!sieve[p]) continue;
  for (let m = p * p; m <= n; m += p) sieve[m] = false;
}
let row = "";
for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
  if (!sieve[i]) continue;
  if (row.length + String(i).length > 7) {
    console.log(row);
    row = "";
  }
  row += (row == "" ? "" : " ") + i;
}
console.log(row);
// Fibonacci, recursive (and slow on purpose)
function fib(n) {
  if (n < 2) return n;
  return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2);
}
for (let i = 0; i <= 15; i++) console.log(fib(i));
// a diamond of stars
const h = 4;
for (let i = 1 - h; i < h; i++) {
  const w = h - (i < 0 ? -i : i);
  console.log(" ".repeat(h - w) + "*".repeat(2 * w - 1));
}
// the towers of Hanoi: every move for 4 disks
let moves = 0;
function hanoi(n, from, to, via) {
  if (n == 0) return;
  hanoi(n - 1, from, via, to);
  moves++;
  if (n >= 3) console.log(n + ":" + from + ">" + to);
  hanoi(n - 1, via, to, from);
}
hanoi(4, "A", "C", "B");
console.log(moves + " moves");
// insertion sort, then a binary search
let a = [42, 7, 19, 3, 88, 25, 61, 14, 50, 9];
for (let i = 1; i < a.length; i++) {
  let x = a[i];
  let j = i - 1;
  while (j >= 0 && a[j] > x) {
    a[j + 1] = a[j];
    j--;
  }
  a[j + 1] = x;
}
function find(v) {
  let lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
  while (lo <= hi) {
    const mid = lo + (hi - lo - (hi - lo) % 2) / 2;
    if (a[mid] == v) return mid;
    if (a[mid] < v) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;
  }
  return -1;
}
for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 3)
  console.log(a.slice(i, i + 3).join());
console.log("61 at " + find(61));
// a binary search tree of objects
function insert(t, k) {
  if (t === null) return {k: k, l: null, r: null};
  if (k < t.k) t.l = insert(t.l, k);
  else t.r = insert(t.r, k);
  return t;
}
function walk(t, out) {
  if (t === null) return out;
  walk(t.l, out); out.push(t.k);
  return walk(t.r, out);
}
function depth(t) {
  if (t === null) return 0;
  const l = depth(t.l), r = depth(t.r);
  return 1 + (l > r ? l : r);
}
let root = null, ks = [50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80, 35, 65];
for (let i = 0; i < ks.length; i++) root = insert(root, ks[i]);
const out = walk(root, []);
for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i += 2)
  console.log(out.slice(i, i + 2).join(" "));
console.log("depth " + depth(root));
// a Caesar cipher on strings
function shift(s, k) {
  let r = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    const c = s.charCodeAt(i);
    if (c >= 65 && c <= 90)
      r += String.fromCharCode((c - 65 + k + 26) % 26 + 65);
    else r += s.charAt(i);
  }
  return r;
}
const words = ["HAL", "CSS", "VMS", "OK"];
for (let i = 0; i < words.length; i++) {
  const w = shift(words[i], 1);
  console.log(words[i] + ">" + w);
}
console.log(shift(shift("ROUND", 13), 13));
// Collatz: the longest chain below 30
let best = 0, arg = 0;
for (let n = 1; n < 30; n++) {
  let x = n, steps = 0;
  while (x != 1) {
    x = x % 2 == 0 ? x / 2 : 3 * x + 1;
    steps++;
  }
  if (steps > best) {
    best = steps;
    arg = n;
    console.log(n + ":" + steps);
  }
}
console.log("max " + arg);
// objects as records, switch on commands
let acct = {owner: "Ada", balance: 100, log: []};
function apply(op, amt) {
  switch (op) {
    case "dep":
      acct.balance += amt;
      break;
    case "wd":
      if (amt > acct.balance) return "no";
      acct.balance -= amt;
      break;
    default:
      return "??";
  }
  acct.log.push(op);
  return "ok";
}
const ops = [["dep", 50], ["wd", 30], ["wd", 500], ["x", 1]];
for (let i = 0; i < ops.length; i++) {
  console.log(ops[i][0] + " " + apply(ops[i][0], ops[i][1]));
}
console.log("bal " + acct.balance);
console.log(acct.log.join());
// closures: each counter keeps its own n
function counter(step) {
  let n = 0;
  return () => { n += step; return n; };
}
const a = counter(1), b = counter(10);
a(); a(); b();
console.log(a(), b());
const add = x => y => x + y;
const inc = add(1);
console.log(inc(41));

// prototypes: methods shared along a chain
function Animal(name, sound) {
  this.name = name;
  this.sound = sound;
}
Animal.prototype.speak = function () {
  return this.name + ": " + this.sound;
};
const cat = new Animal("cat", "meow");
const dog = new Animal("dog", "woof");
console.log(cat.speak());
console.log(dog.speak());
const pup = Object.create(dog);
pup.sound = "yip";
console.log(pup.speak());
console.log(pup.hasOwnProperty("name"));
const say = dog.speak.bind(cat);
console.log(say());
for (let k in pup) console.log(k);
// async / await: each await lets the others run
async function count(name, n) {
  for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
    console.log(name + i);
    await null;
  }
  return name + " done";
}
count("a", 3).then(v => console.log(v));
count("b", 2).then(v => console.log(v));
console.log("main");
const later = new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500));
later.then(() => console.log("timer"));

Lines past 24 are not read.

A pasted code block shows and runs as one line. If it had several, undo (Ctrl+Z, or ⌘Z on a Mac) and paste it as plain text: Ctrl+Shift+V, or ⌥⇧⌘V on a Mac.

Everything below the editor happens in CSS. When you press Run, a font reads your text back (a variable axis makes HarfBuzz copy the code of one column into an invisible glyph's width, and a scan sweeps the columns, one per frame). Then the compiler, a stylesheet, runs over those characters: a lexer on a chain of one element per character, then a parser on a chain of one element per token, each parser rule picked by a container query. Every instruction word it emits is an element named after its RAM cell. Then the CPU, also a stylesheet, runs the program: each layout pass executes up to 32 instructions of a register machine as a chain of nested elements, out of a cache of RAM held in custom properties. Output appears in the console on the left.

The language is a small JavaScript subset: var, function, if/else, while, for, switch, return, integer arithmetic, strings, arrays, objects, console.log(x) and putc(c). Up to 24 lines of 64 columns (the faint line marks the edge); paste as plain text. Run scans the editor once (about a second), then compiles; Edit clears the machine. The chips above the editor switch to a sample program; each keeps your edits.
